questions.text: What does the study of Geography primarily involve?
questions.explanation: Geography studies the Earth and its physical and human features.

questions.text: What is the true shape of the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Earth is slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator, making it a geoid.

questions.text: How long does the Earth take to complete one rotation on its axis?
questions.explanation: The Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours, causing day and night.

questions.text: What does latitude measure on the Earth's surface?
options: Distance east or west of Greenwich
Distance north or south of the Equator
questions.explanation: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator.

questions.text: The Greenwich Meridian represents which line of longitude?
questions.explanation: The Greenwich Meridian is the prime meridian at 0° longitude.

questions.text: What does the scale of a map represent?
options: The ratio of map distance to ground distance
questions.explanation: Map scale is the ratio between distance on the map and actual distance on the ground.

questions.text: How are igneous rocks formed from molten material or cooling magma?
options: By cooling and solidification of molten material
By heat and pressure on existing rocks
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools and solidifies.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge (pluviometer) measures the amount of rainfall.

questions.text: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about one-third of the Earth's surface.

questions.text: The River Nile flows through which continent?
questions.explanation: The River Nile is the longest river in Africa.

questions.text: How is the concept of population density defined in geography?
options: Number of people per unit area
questions.explanation: Population density is the number of people living per unit area, usually per km².

questions.text: Lagos is the largest city in which country?
questions.explanation: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria and one of the largest in Africa.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary economic activity?
questions.explanation: Farming is a primary activity because it involves direct exploitation of natural resources.

questions.text: Petroleum is mainly found in which region of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's petroleum reserves are concentrated in the Niger Delta region.

questions.text: What do contour lines on a topographic map represent?
options: Lines of equal height above sea level
questions.explanation: Contour lines join points of equal height above sea level.

questions.text: What does the acronym GIS stand for in full?
questions.explanation: GIS stands for Geographic Information System, used for storing and analysing spatial data.

questions.text: Desertification is most common in which part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Desertification mainly affects the northern part of Nigeria, especially the Sahel region.

questions.text: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable because it is continuously replenished by the sun.

questions.text: Nigeria is located in which region of Africa?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is the most populous country in West Africa.

questions.text: What is the time difference between two places separated by 15° of longitude?
questions.explanation: The Earth rotates 15° per hour, so 15° equals 1 hour time difference.

questions.text: Which branch of geography deals with the study of landforms?
questions.explanation: Geomorphology is the study of landforms and the processes that shape them.

questions.text: How long does the Earth take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Earth takes approximately 365¼ days to revolve around the Sun.

questions.text: What is the main cause of the seasons on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted at 23½°, causing different parts to receive varying amounts of sunlight.

questions.text: What is the Prime Meridian also known as?
questions.explanation: The Prime Meridian at 0° longitude passes through Greenwich, London.

questions.text: At what latitude is the Tropic of Cancer located?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is at 23½° north of the Equator.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a large scale map in mathematics?
options: A map covering a very large area with little detail
A map covering a small area with much detail
A map of the whole world
A map with no scale bar
questions.explanation: A large scale map shows a small area in great detail, e.g. 1:10,000.

questions.text: Closely spaced contour lines on a map indicate:
questions.explanation: Closely spaced contour lines show steep slopes because height changes over a short distance.

questions.text: Which of the following is a sedimentary rock?
questions.explanation: Limestone is formed from the accumulation and compaction of sediments, usually shells and coral.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of measured by a barometer in mathematics?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric (air) pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
questions.explanation: Population is not a weather element; weather elements include temperature, pressure, humidity, etc.

questions.text: The hottest latitude zone on Earth is the:
questions.explanation: The Torrid zone between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn receives the most direct sunlight.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a tropical rainforest climate?
options: High temperature and heavy rainfall throughout the year
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforest (Af) climate has high temperatures and rainfall throughout the year.

questions.text: Which vegetation type is found in the Guinea Savanna of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Guinea Savanna has tall grasses with scattered drought-resistant trees.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cloud type found at high altitude?
questions.explanation: Cirrus clouds are thin, wispy clouds found at high altitudes above 6,000m.

questions.text: What is the main cause of convectional rainfall?
options: Rising warm moist air that cools and condenses
questions.explanation: Convectional rainfall occurs when the sun heats the ground, causing air to rise, cool, and condense.

questions.text: Which type of rock is formed by heat and pressure applied to existing rocks?
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are changed by intense heat and pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Earthquakes are mainly caused by?
options: Movement along fault lines in the Earth's crust
questions.explanation: Most earthquakes result from sudden movement along geological faults in the Earth's crust.

questions.text: Which of the following is a erosional river landform?
questions.explanation: A V-shaped valley is formed by vertical erosion by rivers in their upper course.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a delta in mathematics?
options: Triangular deposit of sediment at a river mouth
questions.explanation: A delta is a triangular-shaped landform built by deposition of sediment where a river meets the sea.

questions.text: The Gulf of Guinea current is mainly a:
questions.explanation: The Guinea Current is a warm ocean current flowing along the West African coast.

questions.text: Tides in the ocean are mainly caused by:
options: The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun
questions.explanation: Tides result from the gravitational attraction of the Moon and Sun on ocean water.

questions.text: Which of the following is an ocean resource?
questions.explanation: Fish and other marine organisms are important biological resources from the ocean.

questions.text: What is meant by population distribution?
options: The way people are spread across an area
The birth rate of a country
The number of males vs females
questions.explanation: Population distribution refers to how people are spread across different parts of an area.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Rural-urban migration refers to?
options: Movement from one country to another
questions.explanation: Rural-urban migration is the movement of people from villages to towns and cities.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a rural settlement?
questions.explanation: Rural settlements are characterised by farming and low population density.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of subsistence agriculture in mathematics?
options: Farming to feed one's family with little or no surplus
questions.explanation: Subsistence agriculture involves growing food mainly for the farmer's own consumption.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cash crop grown in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cocoa is a major cash crop grown in Nigeria for export, especially in the south-west.

questions.text: A plantation farm is characterised by:
options: Large-scale production of a single cash crop
questions.explanation: Plantations are large estates that specialise in growing one cash crop for export.

questions.text: Which mineral is mined in Jos, Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Jos and the surrounding Plateau area are known for tin mining.

questions.text: Which of the following is a manufacturing industry?
questions.explanation: Textile production is a secondary (manufacturing) industry that processes raw materials.

questions.text: Which form of transportation is cheapest for moving heavy goods over long distances?
questions.explanation: Water transport is the cheapest mode for carrying bulky goods over long distances.

questions.text: Which of the following is a means of communication?
questions.explanation: Television is a mass medium used for the transmission of information.

questions.text: World trade is important because it allows countries to:
options: Specialise in goods they produce best
questions.explanation: International trade allows countries to specialise in comparative advantage goods.

questions.text: Which of the following is an indicator of economic development?
questions.explanation: High GDP per capita indicates a higher standard of living and economic development.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of deforestation in mathematics?
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the large-scale removal or destruction of forest cover.

questions.text: Which of the following is a consequence of flooding?
questions.explanation: Flooding causes loss of life, destruction of property, and displacement of people.

questions.text: Which natural disaster involves a sudden shaking of the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: An earthquake is a sudden tremor or vibration caused by movement in the Earth's crust.

questions.text: What does the technique of remote sensing involve in geographic study?
options: Collecting information about the Earth from a distance
Walking through an area to map it
questions.explanation: Remote sensing is the collection of data about the Earth's surface from satellites or aircraft.

questions.text: Which river is the longest in Africa?
questions.explanation: The River Nile at approximately 6,650 km is the longest river in Africa.

questions.text: Which of these Nigerian cities is the current capital?
questions.explanation: Abuja replaced Lagos as the capital of Nigeria in 1991.

questions.text: Which branch of geography studies the relationship between humans and their environment?
questions.explanation: Human geography examines how humans interact with and modify their environment.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a compass in map reading?
questions.explanation: A compass is used to determine direction and orientation on a map.

questions.text: The Earth revolves around the Sun in which direction?
questions.explanation: The Earth revolves around the Sun from west to east.

questions.text: What is the imaginary line that divides the Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator at 0° latitude divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.text: Places on the same meridian have the same:
questions.explanation: All places on the same meridian have the same longitude and local time.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A statement scale is expressed as?
questions.explanation: A statement scale uses words, e.g. '1 centimetre represents 1 kilometre'.

questions.text: Which conventional sign is typically used to represent a river on a map?
questions.explanation: Rivers and water bodies are typically shown in blue on topographic maps.

questions.text: A spur on a hillside is shown on a contour map by contours that:
questions.explanation: On a contour map, spurs are shown where contour lines bend towards lower ground (valley).

questions.text: To find the bearing of place B from place A on a map, you measure the angle from:
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from true north.

questions.text: Which of the following rocks is used as a building material in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Granite, an igneous rock, is widely used as a building and construction material.

questions.text: The process by which rocks are broken down by natural agents is called:
questions.explanation: Weathering is the breakdown of rocks in situ by physical, chemical, or biological agents.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of mechanical weathering?
questions.explanation: Root growth exerts pressure on rocks and physically breaks them apart.

questions.text: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust through which:
questions.explanation: Volcanoes are vents through which molten rock (magma/lava) and gases are ejected.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a flood plain?
options: A flat area of land alongside a river
questions.explanation: A flood plain is a flat area of land on either side of a river, formed by repeated flooding.

questions.text: Which ocean current flows along the west coast of North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Canary Current is a cold current that flows southward along the coast of northwest Africa.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an atoll in mathematics?
options: A ring-shaped coral reef surrounding a lagoon
questions.explanation: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef that encircles a lagoon, often formed from a sinking volcanic island.

questions.text: Which of the following factors affects population distribution?
questions.explanation: Climate, terrain, water availability, and economic opportunities affect where people settle.

questions.text: The push factor in migration refers to:
questions.explanation: Push factors are negative conditions (e.g. poverty, conflict) that cause people to leave an area.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A conurbation is formed when?
options: Several towns and cities merge into one large urban area
questions.explanation: A conurbation is a large metropolitan area formed when several cities merge together.

questions.text: Which type of farming involves growing crops and rearing animals together?
questions.explanation: Mixed farming combines crop production and animal rearing on the same farm.

questions.text: Rubber is mainly grown in which part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Rubber plantations are mainly found in the rainforest belt of southern Nigeria.

questions.text: Which of the following is a problem of mining in Africa?
questions.explanation: Mining causes environmental degradation, water pollution, and destruction of farmland.

questions.text: Which of the following is a factor affecting the location of industries?
options: Proximity to raw materials and market
questions.explanation: Industries are located near raw materials, markets, labour, and transport routes.

questions.text: Pipeline transportation in Nigeria is mainly used to move:
questions.explanation: Pipelines in Nigeria transport crude oil and refined petroleum products.

questions.text: Which international organisation helps promote world trade?
questions.explanation: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) deals with the rules of trade between nations.

questions.text: What is the term for the total value of goods and services produced in a country per year?
questions.explanation: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country.

questions.text: Which of the following is an effect of deforestation?
questions.explanation: Removing trees exposes soil to erosion and reduces the land's ability to absorb water, causing floods.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of desertification in mathematics?
options: The spread of desert conditions into previously fertile land
questions.explanation: Desertification is the degradation of land in arid and semi-arid areas due to climate and human activities.

questions.text: Which of the following is an air pollutant?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide from vehicle exhausts is a major air pollutant harmful to health.

questions.text: What is conservation of natural resources?
options: The careful management and protection of natural resources
questions.explanation: Conservation means using natural resources wisely to ensure they last for future generations.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A tsunami is caused by?
questions.explanation: Tsunamis are large ocean waves triggered by undersea earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides.

questions.text: Which type of rainfall is common in equatorial regions?
questions.explanation: Convectional rainfall is common in equatorial regions due to intense solar heating.

questions.text: Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to rise over:
questions.explanation: Orographic (relief) rainfall occurs when air is forced upward over mountains, cooling and condensing.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the tropical grassland (Savanna) climate?
questions.explanation: The Savanna climate has a wet season and a dry season with scattered grassland vegetation.

questions.text: The tropical rainforest in Nigeria is located mainly in the:
questions.explanation: The tropical rainforest belt lies across southern Nigeria, from Lagos to the Cross River area.

questions.text: Which of the following is an agent of transportation?
questions.explanation: Wind, water, ice, and gravity are all agents that transport weathered materials.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a meander in mathematics?
options: A bend in the course of a river
questions.explanation: Meanders are bends in a river formed by lateral erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank.

questions.text: The continental shelf is the gently sloping submerged part of a continent. It is important for:
questions.explanation: Continental shelves are rich in fish stocks and often contain oil and gas deposits.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a fjord?
options: A deep narrow sea inlet between cliffs, formed by glacial erosion
questions.explanation: A fjord is a long, narrow sea inlet with steep sides, carved by glaciers.

questions.text: Which of the following is a factor that influences climate?
questions.explanation: Altitude, latitude, ocean currents, and distance from the sea all influence climate.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A hygrometer is used to measure?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures the amount of moisture (humidity) in the air.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a type of rock?
questions.explanation: Mineral is not a rock type. The three main rock types are igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Lava is molten rock that?
options: Flows out onto the Earth's surface
questions.explanation: Lava is magma that has reached the Earth's surface through volcanic eruptions.

questions.text: Which of these is a fold mountain in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains in North Africa were formed by the folding of rock layers during tectonic movements.

questions.text: Which of the following landforms is created by deposition at a river mouth?
questions.explanation: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment at its mouth where it meets a body of water.

questions.text: The International Date Line roughly follows which longitude?
questions.explanation: The International Date Line approximately follows the 180° meridian in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of standard time in mathematics?
options: The local time at every town
The time adopted by a country based on a standard meridian
The time at the North Pole
questions.explanation: Standard time is the uniform time adopted by a country based on its chosen standard meridian.

questions.text: Which of the following is a conventional sign for a railway on a map?
questions.explanation: Railways are typically shown as a black line with small cross-ties resembling railway sleepers.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Aerial photographs are taken from?
questions.explanation: Aerial photographs are taken from aircraft, drones, or satellites to show large areas from above.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes an oasis?
options: A fertile area with water in a desert
questions.explanation: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where water is available, often from an underground spring.

questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of irrigation in agriculture?
options: It eliminates the need for soil
It allows farming in dry areas
It replaces the need for seeds
questions.explanation: Irrigation supplies water to crops in areas where rainfall is insufficient for farming.

questions.text: Which type of erosion is caused by running water?
questions.explanation: River erosion occurs when flowing water wears away rock and soil along river channels.

questions.text: Which ocean separates Africa from the Americas?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic Ocean lies between the Americas to the west and Europe/Africa to the east.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a plateau in mathematics?
options: An extensive flat area of high land
questions.explanation: A plateau is a large area of relatively flat, elevated land.

questions.text: The Jos Plateau in Nigeria is known for mining which mineral?
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau is famous for tin and columbite mining in Nigeria.

questions.text: Which of the following is an effect of ocean currents on climate?
options: Warm currents increase temperature and humidity
questions.explanation: Warm ocean currents raise temperatures and increase humidity along adjacent coastlines.

questions.text: What is the main cause of urbanisation in developing countries?
options: Rural-urban migration for jobs and services
People moving from cities to farms
Natural increase in rural areas only
questions.explanation: People move from rural areas to cities seeking better employment, education, and healthcare.

questions.text: Which of the following is a social amenity found in urban areas?
questions.explanation: Hospitals and schools are social amenities (services) typically provided in urban centres.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major problem of urban areas in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Urban areas in Nigeria face traffic congestion, inadequate housing, and poor sanitation.

questions.text: The branch of geography that deals with maps and chart-making is called:
questions.explanation: Cartography is the science and art of making maps.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the lithosphere in mathematics?
options: The solid outer layer of the Earth
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the rigid outer layer of the Earth comprising the crust and upper mantle.

questions.text: The Tropic of Capricorn is located at:
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn is at 23½° south of the Equator.

questions.text: Which zone of the atmosphere is closest to the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere where all weather occurs.

questions.text: What is the best definition of a grid reference on a map?
options: A set of numbers locating a point using grid lines
The name of the map maker
questions.explanation: A grid reference uses eastings and northings to locate a point on a map.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a small-scale map?
options: A map with much detail of a small area
A map covering a large area with less detail
questions.explanation: A small-scale map shows a large area with less detail, e.g. 1:1,000,000.

questions.text: Contour intervals on a map represent:
options: The vertical difference in height between adjacent contour lines
questions.explanation: Contour interval is the difference in height between two adjacent contour lines.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the rock cycle in mathematics?
options: The continuous process by which rocks are formed, broken down, and reformed
A type of road made of rocks
A wheel used to transport stones
questions.explanation: The rock cycle describes how rocks change from one type to another over geological time.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Obsidian is a type of?
questions.explanation: Obsidian is a dark volcanic glass formed from rapidly cooled lava.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a waterfall?
options: Steep vertical drop of water along a river course
questions.explanation: A waterfall occurs where a river flows over a vertical or steep drop in its channel.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A gorge is formed by?
options: Deep vertical erosion by a river
questions.explanation: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, formed by vertical river erosion.

questions.text: The lagoon along the coast of Lagos was formed by:
options: Sand bar or barrier island cutting off part of the sea
questions.explanation: Lagos Lagoon was formed when a sand bar separated a portion of the sea from the ocean.

questions.text: What is the main cause of tidal bores in rivers?
options: Strong tidal flow pushing upstream against the river current
questions.explanation: Tidal bores occur when a strong incoming tide pushes water upstream against the river's flow.

questions.text: The Sahara Desert is located in which part of Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert covers most of North Africa, the world's largest hot desert.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the vegetation of the Sahel region?
questions.explanation: The Sahel has sparse grassland and scattered shrubs adapted to very dry conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following is a consequence of overgrazing?
questions.explanation: Overgrazing removes vegetation cover, leading to soil erosion and desertification.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a crater lake in mathematics?
options: A lake formed by river damming
A lake formed in the mouth of a dormant volcano
questions.explanation: A crater lake fills the depression (caldera) at the top of a volcano.

questions.text: Which of the following factors determines the density of drainage in an area?
options: Number of cars on the road
Rainfall amount, rock type and slope
questions.explanation: Drainage density depends on rainfall, permeability of rock, and the gradient of the land.

questions.text: What is the main product of the Benue River trough?
questions.explanation: The Benue River trough is associated with alluvial tin deposits in Nigeria.

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Snow is a form of precipitation where water vapour freezes into ice crystals and falls.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A cold front occurs when?
options: Warm air pushes cold air away
Cold air moves into an area occupied by warm air
questions.explanation: A cold front forms when cold air advances and replaces warm air, often causing heavy rain.

questions.text: Which of the following is a way of conserving soil?
questions.explanation: Terrace farming reduces the speed of water runoff on slopes, preventing soil erosion.

questions.text: The main occupation of people in the mangrove region of Nigeria is:
questions.explanation: The mangrove swamp region of southern Nigeria is mainly inhabited by fishermen.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major export crop of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Palm oil is one of Nigeria's traditional and major export crops.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of shifting cultivation in mathematics?
options: Clearing and farming a piece of land, then moving to another after a few years
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn) involves farming a plot, then abandoning it when soil fertility drops.

questions.text: The oil palm is mainly grown in which part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Oil palm thrives in the humid rainforest belt of southern Nigeria.

questions.text: Which of the following is a means of land transportation?
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles (cars, trucks, buses) are the most common means of land transportation.

questions.text: Which of the following is a problem of transportation in Nigeria?
options: Poor road networks and insufficient rail lines
questions.explanation: Nigeria faces challenges of poor road conditions, insufficient rail, and inadequate water transport.

questions.text: What is the main function of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)?
options: To give free oil to all countries
To coordinate and unify petroleum policies of member countries
questions.explanation: OPEC coordinates petroleum policies and stabilises oil markets among member nations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a reason for economic development planning?
options: To improve the standard of living of citizens
questions.explanation: Economic development planning aims to improve living standards, healthcare, and education.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of overgrazing in mathematics?
options: Allowing animals to eat small amounts
Keeping too many animals on a piece of land beyond its carrying capacity
questions.explanation: Overgrazing occurs when too many livestock graze on land, destroying vegetation and causing erosion.

questions.text: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Wind energy is renewable because wind is a naturally replenishing resource.

questions.text: The International Date Line is located at approximately:
questions.explanation: The International Date Line follows approximately 180° longitude in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a physical feature?
questions.explanation: A river is a natural (physical) feature of the landscape, unlike human-made structures.

questions.text: What is the Equatorial climate characterised by?
options: High temperatures and heavy rainfall all year
questions.explanation: The Equatorial climate has consistently high temperatures and heavy rainfall throughout the year.

questions.text: The Harmattan wind in West Africa blows from:
options: The north from the Sahara Desert
The east from the Indian Ocean
questions.explanation: The Harmattan is a dry, dusty trade wind that blows from the Sahara Desert over West Africa.

questions.text: Which of the following is caused by the rotation of the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Earth's rotation on its axis causes the cycle of day and night.

questions.text: A map showing only the physical features of an area is called a:
questions.explanation: A physical map shows natural features such as mountains, rivers, and vegetation.

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of erosion by wind?
questions.explanation: Wind erosion involves corrasion (blasting with particles) and deflation (removal of loose particles).

questions.text: The continental divide in Africa separates the drainage of the Atlantic and Indian Ocean basins along:
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley forms a major drainage divide in East Africa.

questions.text: An esker is a ridge of sand and gravel formed by:
options: Meltwater streams flowing under a glacier
questions.explanation: Eskers are winding ridges of sediment deposited by meltwater flowing in tunnels beneath glaciers.

questions.text: What is the significance of the lines of longitude?
options: They help determine time differences between places
questions.explanation: Lines of longitude (meridians) help calculate time differences, since the Earth rotates 15° per hour.

questions.text: An old man on the coast sees a ship approaching. He sees the mast first because:
questions.explanation: The mast appears first due to the curvature of the Earth's surface.

questions.text: Which of the following is a difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather is long-term; climate is short-term
Weather is day-to-day conditions; climate is the average over many years
questions.explanation: Weather refers to short-term atmospheric conditions; climate is the average weather pattern over 30+ years.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments measures wind speed?
questions.explanation: An anemometer is used to measure the speed of the wind.

questions.text: Stratus clouds are characterised by:
options: White, fluffy heaps at high altitude
A uniform grey layer covering the sky like a blanket
questions.explanation: Stratus clouds form a flat, grey, uniform layer low in the sky, often producing drizzle.

questions.text: A cumulonimbus cloud is associated with:
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are tall, dense clouds associated with thunderstorms, heavy rain, and lightning.

questions.text: What is condensation in the water cycle?
options: Water vapour cooling and turning into liquid water droplets
questions.explanation: Condensation is the process where water vapour cools and changes back into tiny liquid droplets.

questions.text: The rock type formed from remains of marine organisms is:
questions.explanation: Chalk is a sedimentary rock formed from the compressed shells and skeletons of marine organisms.

questions.text: A volcano that has not erupted for a long time is called:
questions.explanation: A dormant volcano is one that has not erupted recently but could erupt again in the future.

questions.text: Which process transports sediment along a river bed by rolling and sliding?
questions.explanation: Traction is the process where large particles are rolled or pushed along the river bed by the current.

questions.text: A levee is a natural embankment found along a river. It is formed by:
options: Deposition of coarse sediment during floods
Wind blowing soil to the river
questions.explanation: Levees form when a river deposits coarser sediment on its banks during flood overflow.

questions.text: The main reason the sea level rises near the equator is:
options: The Earth's rotation causes water to bulge at the equator
questions.explanation: The Earth's rotation causes the ocean to bulge slightly at the equator due to centrifugal force.

questions.text: Which of the following countries does the River Niger flow through?
questions.explanation: The River Niger flows through Guinea, Mali, Niger, Benin, and Nigeria before entering the Atlantic.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major oil-producing state in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Rivers State, with Port Harcourt as its capital, is a major oil-producing state in the Niger Delta.

questions.text: What is the main type of farming practised in the northern part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Northern Nigeria is characterised by pastoral nomadism (cattle rearing) and irrigated crop farming.

questions.text: What is an earthquake epicentre and how is it best described?
options: The point deep inside the Earth where the quake starts
The point on the surface directly above the focus
The edge of a tectonic plate
The highest point of a mountain
questions.explanation: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus (hypocentre) of an earthquake.

questions.text: Which of the following is an effect of the Bermuda High on West African climate?
options: It is linked to the West African monsoon and rainfall patterns
questions.explanation: The Bermuda High pressure system influences the monsoon winds that bring rainfall to West Africa.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a peninsula in mathematics?
options: A piece of land almost surrounded by water on three sides
questions.explanation: A peninsula is an area of land that projects into a body of water and is surrounded on three sides.

questions.text: The Great Green Wall initiative in Africa aims to:
options: Create a belt of trees across the Sahel to combat desertification
Construct a highway across the desert
Build the tallest building in the world
questions.explanation: The Great Green Wall is an African-led project to grow a belt of trees across the Sahel to stop desertification.

questions.text: What is the main source of energy for the water cycle?
questions.explanation: The Sun provides the energy that drives evaporation, the first stage of the water cycle.

questions.text: What is a tributary and how is it best described?
options: A river that flows into the sea
A smaller river that joins a larger river
questions.explanation: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger main river.

questions.text: The source of the River Niger is in:
questions.explanation: The River Niger rises in the Guinea Highlands near the Fouta Djallon mountains.

questions.text: Which type of map projection preserves direction but distorts area?
questions.explanation: A gnomonic (azimuthal) projection preserves directions from the centre but distorts area.

questions.text: The process by which plants release water vapour into the atmosphere is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plant leaves into the atmosphere.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes an archipelago?
options: A group or chain of islands
questions.explanation: An archipelago is a group or chain of islands, e.g. the Philippines or the Maldives.

questions.text: The Benue River in Nigeria joins the River Niger at:
questions.explanation: The Benue and Niger rivers meet at Lokoja, Kogi State, forming the main Niger River channel.

questions.text: Which of the following is an effect of global warming?
options: Rising sea levels due to melting ice caps
questions.explanation: Global warming causes glaciers and ice caps to melt, leading to rising sea levels.

questions.text: Which scale would show the most detail on a map?
questions.explanation: 1:50,000 is the largest scale listed and shows the most detail for a given area.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a spit in mathematics?
options: A narrow ridge of sand or shingle projecting from the coast into the sea
questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle extending from the shore into the sea by longshore drift.

questions.text: The Great Rift Valley in East Africa was formed by:
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley was formed by the divergence of tectonic plates causing faulting and subsidence.

questions.text: What is the Tundra climate characterised by?
options: Very low temperatures with permafrost and sparse vegetation
questions.explanation: The Tundra has extremely cold temperatures, permafrost, and very limited plant growth.

questions.text: The Berg Wind in southern Africa is:
options: A hot dry wind blowing from interior highlands to the coast
questions.explanation: The Berg Wind is a hot, dry wind that blows downslope from the interior plateau to the coast.

questions.text: The population census is important because it:
options: Provides data for planning and allocation of resources
questions.explanation: A census provides accurate population data needed for government planning and resource distribution.

questions.text: Which of the following is a push factor for rural-urban migration?
options: Availability of good schools in cities
Lack of employment opportunities in rural areas
questions.explanation: Lack of jobs in rural areas pushes people to move to cities in search of employment.

questions.text: Which of the following is a commercial farming activity in West Africa?
options: Keeping a few chickens at home
questions.explanation: Commercial farming involves large-scale production for sale and export, like rubber plantations.

questions.text: Which type of rock is most suitable for making cement?
questions.explanation: Limestone is the primary raw material used in the manufacture of cement.

questions.text: The continental shelf is important for fishing because it:
options: Has shallow, sunlit water that supports marine life
questions.explanation: The shallow waters of the continental shelf allow sunlight to penetrate, supporting abundant marine life.

questions.text: A lighthouse is built on a coast primarily to:
options: Warn and guide ships away from dangerous shorelines
questions.explanation: Lighthouses emit light to warn ships of dangerous coasts and guide safe navigation.

questions.text: Which of the following is a difference between a map and a photograph?
options: A map always shows more detail than a photo
A map uses symbols and a scale; a photo shows an image from above
questions.explanation: Maps use symbols, scale, and projections to represent features; photographs are direct images.

questions.text: The main reason for studying geography is to:
options: Understand the Earth, its people, and the relationship between them
Learn only how to read maps
questions.explanation: Geography helps us understand the physical world, human activities, and how they interact.
